title: Exceptional coefficient construction: field descent
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R_E$, uniformizers $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed separated over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Fix an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each $E$ use the integral finite-Tor category, the exact $R_E$-linear adjunction $F_R\dashv G_R$ obtained by reduction/limit transport of the etale system adjunction, its prescribed compact-support identification, and its canonical proper/open scalar comparisons. Assume their left maps satisfy balanced scalar identity and composition, and their right maps are the invertible counit transposes. Use raw scalar localization $\mathcal C_{T,E}=\mathcal C_{T,R_E}[1/\varpi_E]$ (same objects and localized Hom modules), and the common finite-subfield category $\mathcal C_{T,\Omega}$ whose objects are pairs $(E,K)$ and whose maps are directed colimits over common finite subfields [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Then the localized $F_E\dashv G_E$ are additive exact adjunctions on exactly the published rational constructible categories: every integral constructible representative has finite Tor amplitude. Their left functor is the published rational compact support, with its identity rational-left realization [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The unit, counit, inverse Hom maps and triangles are the images of the integral ones, with their induced shifts.

There are invertible shift-compatible integral-to-rational and rational scalar comparisons satisfying $\epsilon_tF_t(b)q=T_Y\epsilon_s$. Composing the integral-to-rational $q$ with the rational-left realization gives exactly the localization of the integral-left realization. On every integral representative the rational scalar $q$ is the raw localization of the integral scalar $q$, also on morphisms $h/\varpi_E^r$.

The formulas $(E,K)\mapsto(E,F_EK)$ and $(E,K)\mapsto(E,G_EK)$ define additive exact functors on $\mathcal C_{-,\Omega}$, acting on represented morphisms by their scalar comparisons. Both this action and the natural adjunction Hom bijections are independent of enlargement to a common field and preserve identities and composition. They give an adjunction at $\Omega$ with represented triangles and shifts. At each finite-field inclusion the left comparison is the identity on $(E,F_EK)$ and its counit transpose is the identity on the represented right object; these comparisons satisfy the same counit and shift equations. No Karoubi completion or unrestricted ambient $\Omega$ adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: For either $T=X,Y$, every object $K$ of the published integral constructible category has bounded residue reduction $K_1$. Choose its cohomological interval $[a,b]$. The residue Tor theorem gives Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for every $K_n$, hence $D^b_c(T,R_E)=D^b_{ctf}(T,R_E)$. Its statement allows arbitrary schemes with $\ell$ invertible, so no absolute separatedness is used. Thus the given integral operations are defined on every object whose raw localization defines the published rational category.

source.place: Integral representatives in the rationalization paragraph; retained returned step 17.

proof.text: Write $Q_{T,E}$ for raw localization. Apply semilinear localization with $R=S=R_E$, $t=u=\varpi_E$ and the identity ring map to $F_R,G_R$. It gives additive exact functors $F_E,G_E$, with their localized shift maps, acting by $F_E(h/\varpi_E^r)=F_R(h)/\varpi_E^r$ and similarly for $G$. Localize the integral unit and counit as natural transformations. The equations $G_R\epsilon_R\circ\eta_RG_R=1$ and $\epsilon_RF_R\circ F_R\eta_R=1$ remain equations because localization preserves composition and whiskering. Explicit inverse Hom maps are $v/\varpi_E^r\mapsto (G_R(v)\eta_R)/\varpi_E^r$ and $w/\varpi_E^r\mapsto(\epsilon_RF_R(w))/\varpi_E^r$; they are well-defined by linearity and inverse by these equations. The natural-bijection theorem gives the desired adjunction, with precisely $Q\eta_R,Q\epsilon_R$. Its units, counits and both triangle identities commute with the localized shifts, since their integral shift equations also localize.

source.place: Rationalization of the integral adjunction; retained step 17.

proof.text: Use the supplied normalized integral left realization $u_R:F_R\cong P_R$, where $P_R$ is the prescribed reduction-tower compact support. Choose its literal normalized presentation $F_R=P_R$ before localization; if the transported presentation is retained, identify it through $Q u_R$ throughout. By the definition of rational compact support its rational left realization is then the identity $F_E=Q P_R$. The integral-to-rational comparison $q_0:Q_YF_R\cong F_EQ_X$ is the identity in the normalized presentation (in the transported presentation it is $Q u_R$ followed by the inverse rational-left realization). Thus composing $q_0$ with the rational-left realization is exactly $Q u_R$. The right comparison $b_0$ is identity on $Q_XG_R$. Its counit equation is the localized counit identity; if left presentations are changed, the counit is changed by precomposition with $(Q u_R)^{-1}$, so the same equation still holds. This also fixes the shifts of these identifications.

source.place: Integral-left and rational-left normalization, retained step 18.

proof.text: For $E\subset L$ apply semilinear localization to the supplied integral scalar functor $T_{L/E}$ and its $q,b$. The image of $\varpi_E$ is invertible in $L$: it is a unit times $\varpi_L^e$. On a fraction the scalar functor sends $h/\varpi_E^r$ to $Q_L(T_{L/E}h)\,\varpi_E^{-r}$. This is exactly the rational scalar functor in the published definition. Define $q_{L/E},b_{L/E}$ by the localized integral components, with the same left realizations as in step 3. Naturality holds on fractions by the semilinear localization theorem, not just on integral arrows. It preserves invertibility, shifts and the equation $\epsilon_L F_L(b)q=T_Y\epsilon_E$. In particular the rational $q$ on integral representatives and all fractions is exactly the raw image of the prescribed integral $q$, and identity and balanced composition equations for $q$ remain true.

source.place: Rational coefficient comparisons on actual integral representatives; retained step 18.

proof.text: The supplied right integral comparison is the mate of $q^{-1}$. The same is true after localization by its counit equation. Apply mate pasting (1) to $q_{L/E}^{-1},q_{M/L}^{-1}$, with the balanced scalar associators, and mate identity (4) at $E=E$. The left identity and composition laws therefore give the right identity and composition laws for $b$. The mate unit equation gives $b_{F_EK}T_X\eta_{E,K}=G_L(q_K^{-1})\eta_{L,T_XK}$. Together with the counit equation this says that both adjunction maps preserve scalar transport. All these are identities for the same specified comparisons, rather than arbitrary choices of right-adjoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Coherence and unit normalization of common-field transitions; retained step 19.

proof.text: Apply coherent pair-functor descent to the finite-field families $F_E$ with comparison $q$, and $G_E$ with comparison $b$. The diagram hypotheses on the coefficient categories (literal identity transitions $T_{E/E}=1$, associators that are identities at a repeated field, pentagon) are the unit and pentagon equations of the specified scalar-extension data, which are the transitions of the common-field category. The comparison hypotheses $q_{E/E}=1$, $b_{E/E}=1$ and the tower equations are the balanced identity and composition laws of steps 4–5. It produces additive functors $F_\Omega(E,K)=(E,F_EK)$ and $G_\Omega(E,M)=(E,G_EM)$. For a represented arrow $[L,h]:(E,K)\to(E',K')$ their actions are respectively $[L,q_{L/E',K'}^{-1}F_L(h)q_{L/E,K}]$ and $[L,b_{L/E',K'}^{-1}G_L(h)b_{L/E,K}]$. The cited descent theorem proves independence of representatives and enlargement, and preservation of identities, addition and composition for precisely these formulas. Only its assertion about the pair categories is used.

source.place: Represented action on common finite fields; retained step 19.

proof.text: For $K=(E,K_E)$ and $M=(E',M_{E'})$, pass to a common finite $L$ and put $K_L=T_{L/E}K_E$, $M_L=T_{L/E'}M_{E'}$. Identify an arrow $a:F_\Omega K\to M$ with $a_L:F_LK_L\to M_L$ by $q$, and send it to the class represented by $\Psi_L(a_L)=G_L(a_L)\eta_{L,K_L}:K_L\to G_LM_L$, identified by $b$ with $K\to G_\Omega M$. The inverse sends $w_L$ to $\epsilon_{L,M_L}F_L(w_L)$. These recipes respect enlargement: for $T=T_{N/L}$ the transported left arrow is $T(a_L)q_{N/L,K_L}^{-1}$, and its transpose is $b_{N/L,M_L}T(\Psi_L(a_L))$ by naturality of $b$ and the unit equation in step 5. The inverse respects enlargement by the counit equation. Equality of representatives is equality at a later common field, so both recipes are well-defined on the Hom colimits. Their composites are identity already at $L$; naturality for arbitrary represented arrows follows by moving those arrows to the same field and applying naturality of $\Psi_L$. The natural-bijection theorem now gives $F_\Omega\dashv G_\Omega$, with unit $[E,\eta_E]$, counit $[E,\epsilon_E]$, and represented triangle identities.

source.place: Common-stage Hom bijections and triangles; retained step 19.

proof.text: Descend the finite-field shift comparisons using the transformation part of coherent pair descent: their scalar compatibility was retained in step 4. The unit and counit commute with them since that equation holds for their representatives over each $E$. Each distinguished triangle of the published common-field category is isomorphic to the image of one over some finite $L$. Apply $F_L$ or $G_L$ there; exactness from step 2 makes its image distinguished. The action in step 6 and the descended shifts identify this image with the triangle obtained by $F_\Omega$ or $G_\Omega$. Hence both common-field functors are exact with these shifts.

source.place: Common-stage exactness and shifts; retained step 19.

proof.text: For the inclusion $J_{T,E}:\mathcal C_{T,E}\to\mathcal C_{T,\Omega}$, the objects $J_{Y,E}F_EK$ and $F_\Omega J_{X,E}K$ are literally the same pair $(E,F_EK)$. On an $E$-arrow both functors have the same action by the identity scalar comparison in step 5. Take their comparison to be identity. Likewise $J_{X,E}G_EM=G_\Omega J_{Y,E}M=(E,G_EM)$. The common-field counit at this object is represented by $\epsilon_{E,M}$, so the identity right comparison satisfies the counit equation and is the unique transpose of the identity left comparison. Shift compatibility holds because both shift comparisons are represented by the same finite-field comparison. Finally the published closed compact-support object is $(E,P_EK)$ by definition, which is the left object just constructed. These choices establish the asserted normalization without adding any objects to either coefficient category.
